# SVG Downloader — full reference for language models

Site: https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/
Source: https://github.com/Flozad/svg-downloader (MIT)
Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-web-downloader-extrac/jfgljaebonkbegekbcfbiojgkjlbhpjn

This file restates the site's substance in one place so it can be answered from
without crawling every page. The canonical wording always lives on the HTML page
each section links to.

---

## What it is

SVG Downloader (store name: "SVG Web Downloader & Extractor") is a free,
open-source Chrome extension. It scans the page you are looking at, finds the
SVGs on it, previews each one in isolation, and saves the original vector file —
one at a time, or the whole page as a ZIP.

It exists because a browser will not hand you an SVG. `Save image as…` only
appears for things the browser treats as images, so an inline `<svg>` — which is
part of the document, with no address of its own — has no such menu at all. An
SVG behind a CSS `background-image` cannot be dragged. A sprite sheet packs
dozens of glyphs into one file. The usual workarounds are screenshotting the icon
(giving a fixed-size raster) or digging the node out of DevTools (giving markup
that often will not open, see `xmlns` below).

## The four sources it detects

1. **Inline `<svg>`** — read straight from the live DOM.
   https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/features/inline-svg
2. **`<img>` and `<object>` vectors**, including `data:` URIs.
3. **CSS `background-image` SVGs** — resolved from computed style, both `url()`
   references and inline `data:` URIs.
   https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/features/css-background-svg
4. **Same-document sprite `<use>` references** — each `<use href="#icon">` is
   resolved back to the single symbol it points at, so you get the one glyph
   rather than the whole sheet.
   https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/features/svg-sprite-extractor

All four appear in the same popup, in one count.

## Using it

https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/docs/usage

1. Navigate to the page and click the SVG Downloader toolbar button. It reads the
   tab only at that moment, scanning the current DOM — so let the page finish
   loading first.
2. Read the count the popup reports; it covers all four sources above.
3. Page through the previews with Previous / Next. Each SVG is rendered lifted
   off the page so it is actually visible.
4. Optionally type a filename for the current SVG. Left blank, it falls back to a
   numbered `svg-1.svg` using the prefix set in the extension's options.
5. **Download Current SVG** saves the one on screen.
6. **Download All as ZIP** bundles every detected SVG, numbered `svg-1.svg`
   upward in page order, de-duplicated. Anything that could not be fetched is
   named in the popup's status line — e.g. `Downloaded 8 of 10 SVGs. Skipped:
   3, 7.` — rather than silently dropped.
   https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/features/bulk-zip-download

## What the download actually is

The saved file is the SVG that was in the page — its paths, its `viewBox`, its
precision — not a re-render and not a screenshot. It stays sharp at any size and
stays editable text.

One repair is applied: inline SVG usually omits `xmlns`, because the HTML parser
supplies it. Saved to a bare file, such markup will not open. SVG Downloader adds
`xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` back automatically, so the file opens in
Figma, Illustrator, VS Code and any browser. This is the usual reason an SVG
copied by hand out of DevTools refuses to open.

## Known limits

- A `<use>` pointing at an **external** sprite file (`<use href="/sprite.svg#cart">`)
  is not resolved and that `<svg>` is skipped. Only same-document references are
  followed, one level deep.
- On pages with more than 10,000 elements the CSS `background-image` scan is
  skipped for speed; the other three sources still report.
- Collection caps at 2,000 inline SVGs, and leaves out any single SVG whose
  markup runs past roughly 2 MB.
- A saved icon can look black. Many icons inherit their colour from CSS through
  `currentColor`, which has nothing to resolve against once the SVG is a
  standalone file. The file is correct; it simply has no colour baked in. The
  extension offers an optional hand-off to the SVG Color Changer to bake one in
  before saving — the single outbound link, followed only if you click it.

## Installing

https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/docs/installation

- From the Chrome Web Store, in one click.
- Or unpacked from source: download the repository, open `chrome://extensions`,
  turn on Developer mode, choose "Load unpacked" and select the extension folder.
  Edge and Brave are the same procedure; only the extensions-page address differs.

Requirements: Chrome 88 or newer, or a current Chromium browser — Microsoft Edge,
Brave. There is no Firefox or Safari build.

## Privacy and permissions

https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/privacy

No page content leaves the browser. Detection, preview and download all run
on-device. There is no server, no account, no upload, no analytics and no
tracking. Two things do go out: SVG assets the page itself already references,
fetched so they can be included in a download; and the optional SVG Color Changer
link, only if clicked.

Your preferences — filename prefix, ZIP name, scan-on-open, and the colour-tool
link — are kept in `chrome.storage.sync`, so they follow your Google Account
across machines. Settings only: never page content, never browsing history.

Four permissions are requested, all narrow:

- `activeTab` and `scripting` — read the current page's DOM, only at the moment
  you open the popup.
- `downloads` — write the files you save.
- `storage` — keep the four preferences above.

There is no background access to your other tabs.

## Cost and licence

Free. No paid tier, no trial, no account. Open source under the MIT licence.

## Comparison

https://svg.clasicwebtools.com/compare/svg-downloader-vs-screenshotting-icons

A screenshot of an icon is a raster stuck at the size it was captured; it blurs
when scaled and cannot be recoloured or edited as shapes. Copying out of DevTools
gets the markup but not the missing namespace, the sprite resolution or the CSS
background case. SVG Downloader returns the vector itself.
